newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Mild profit-taking saps European stocks.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mild profit-taking saps European stocks.

text.p: Mild profit-taking halted the bull run on most European stock markets on Thursday but German floor trade closed at a record high, although London narrowly failed to break the 5,000-point barrier.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar dipped slightly below 1.79 marks in the early afternoon but later recovered a little on positive U.S. economic data.

European markets indeed got off to a storming start, with the Paris CAC-40 index breaking through 3,000 points for the first time and London's FTSE-100 climbing to within seven points of the 5,000 barrier.

But by mid-morning investors decided to cash in on the surge which has carried European bourses to a series of records this week. Wall Street also failed to provide inspiration when it opened slightly weaker on Thursday.
In Germany, the DAX index closed up 26.07 points or 0.62 percent at a record 4,227.31. But even this did not give the full picture as the DAX measures only floor trade which closes at 1200 GMT.
Prices fell in later German electronic trade and the IBIS index, which measures it, was down 0.5 percent at 4,202.69 at mid-afternoon.

The profit-takers were active in London, where blue chips have risen four percent since Monday. "The market is up 160-odd points this week so there is bound to be some profit-taking like this," one market maker said.

But some traders forecast the buyers would soon be back, despite a growing feeling that the bull run is starting to defy economic logic, as British interest rates rise and a strong pound punishes exporters.
"If it (the FTSE) comes down, people will just buy more," another trader said. "The market will probably come back down but it will have another go at 5,000."
At mid-afternoon, the FTSE-100 had slipped from an intra-day record high of 4,993 points and was down 9.3 points at 4,954.9.

In Paris, the CAC-40 index of blue chips stormed through 3,000 points at the opening for the first time. But profit-takers dragged it down to 2,963.65, some 24 points or 0.82 percent lower than the Wednesday close.

The public deficit remained a worry for French investors. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin met ministers on Thursday to discuss budget measures which will be announced on Monday along with an audit of public finances.

After Wednesday's storming performance, Wall Street provided little inspiration on Thursday and the Dow also drifted lower on profit-taking. Swiss shares likewise slipped but markets in Italy and Austria hit records.

On the foreign exchanges, the dollar dipped below 1.79 marks but recovered some lost ground as an index of business activity produced by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia for July far overshot market forecasts.
The dollar stood at 1.7901 marks, down from an early high of 1.8020 and late Wednesday's 1.7980.
Dealers earlier said rumours that the central banks of Italy, Spain and Britain were buying marks for their domestic currencies had checked the dollar's progress.
"It looks more like noise than real activity but the market is hyper-sensitive to any central bank action whether it's intervention or not," said a U.S. bank dealer.
However, dealers said the Italian central bank was buying marks for lire at just under 972 lire to the mark.

The dollar was stable at 116.14 yen compared with 116.27 late on Wednesday in Europe. It was supported by news during earlier Asian trading that the Japanese trade surplus rose over 934 billion yen year-on-year in June compared with a forecast rise of over one trillion yen.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 116.14 yen and 1.7901 marks compared with 116.27 yen and 1.7980 marks in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 9.3 points at 4,954.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade closed up 26.07 points or 0.62 percent at a record 4,227.31. In later electronic trade the IBIS index was down 21 points or 0.5 percent at 4,202.69.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was at 2,963.65, down 24.36 points or 0.82 percent.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $319.40 an ounce compared with a Wednesday afternoon fixing of $319.50. Silver was down 10 cents at $4.22.
